source.title: Towards Irreversible Machine Unlearning for Diffusion Models
source.authors: Xun Yuan; Zi-Long Zhao; Jia-Yu Li; A. Pasikhani; Prosanta Gope; Biplab Sikdar

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a relearning attack and a counter-method in conditional diffusion models, a different model family and setting from the LLM-focused claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures generation of previously unlearned objects/styles after fine-tuning on auxiliary data, and reports results for its proposed counter-method. Its auxiliary data is retain-like or follows the retain distribution; it does not test a few-shot relearning set, quantization, activation-direction ablation, or prompt-only attacks. Cited attacks and findings from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes unlearned conditional diffusion models on target-free auxiliary data and measures how often the unlearned class or style is regenerated. It also tests a counter-method (DiMUM) against this attack. This is a relearning-attack test in a new setting (image diffusion models, not LLMs).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DiMRA reverses finetuning-based unlearning in conditional diffusion models using auxiliary data without the target. They find DiMUM most robust because its convergent loss reaches a new local optimum. They call irreversibility a potential, not established in general.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies conditional diffusion models rather than LLMs. DiMRA fine-tunes unlearned models on auxiliary image/prompt data that excludes the target class or style; DiMUM replaces the target with alternative memorized content.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery changes with unlearning method, number of unlearning steps, target class, and auxiliary-data assumption; the paper reports lower recovery with more unlearning steps and generally lower values under Assumption (ii).
record.problems: The attack results use targeted-class/style classification accuracy as a proxy for regeneration. Results vary by target, method, unlearning duration, and auxiliary-data assumption. No uncertainty estimates are stated. This is evidence on diffusion models, not LLMs.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports ARDiMRA for the UnlearnCanvas feature/style experiment in Table IV (6 methods × 3 unlearning durations), as well as unlearning ARMU and FID measurements. These additional results were not extracted because the 60-row limit was reached with the CIFAR-10 attack results; no results from Tables II or III were omitted.

untested.parts: LLM knowledge unlearning. Prompt, quantization and internal-edit attacks.
Few-example relearning sets, a subset of the forgotten data, loosely related data, set-size variation, LLMs.
Entire version: no activation ablation or block-vs-delete analysis (only a loss-convergence argument).
Entire version: no prompt-only attacks (adversarial prompting is only cited).
DiMUM is tested only against DiMRA; no prompt, quantization or internal-edit attacks; no LLMs.

missing.what: UnlearnCanvas Van Gogh style unlearning on SD v1.5. ARDiMRA for CA/ESD/Ediff is 0.91–1 even at 5K steps; Salun 0.78/0.39/0.09 and SHS 0.60/0.35/0.12 at 1K/2K/5K; DiMUM 0.17/0.02/0.01. All methods have ARMU ≈ 0 before attack.
About 400 attack steps suffice to reverse CA, ESD and Ediff.
DiMUM at 40K unlearning steps: ARDiMRA below 6% for bird, cat and deer.
FID/sFID after unlearning. Sfront degrades generation (e.g., Auto FID 39.07 vs 17.92 Salun); DiMUM has the lowest FID.

record.verdict_notes: Diffusion-model setting, so evidence on LLM unlearning is indirect. Rows are linked under T3 as analogues of A/B/F. DiMUM rows were moved to F, since they test the counter-method rather than standard unlearning. Recovery is measured by a classifier on 1000 generated images, takes the maximum over 60K attack steps, and reports no uncertainty. The auxiliary data is large (retain or test set), not a small relearning set.

versions.untested_parts: Tests whether fine-tuning attacks recover targeted generation after reported unlearning, but does not establish near-chance performance together with preserved general ability for every method and setting as a single combined criterion.
Tests fine-tuning on auxiliary data without the target class/style, but not a few-example set, a subset of forgotten facts, or loosely related examples at varying set sizes.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No prompt-only rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery attack.
Tests DiMUM against the paper's DiMRA relearning attack only; it does not test robustness against activation edits, quantization, or prompt-only attacks.

Table IV (SD v1.5 UnlearnCanvas, Van Gogh style, 10K attack steps) is not in the rows: CA/ESD/Ediff 0.91-1; Salun 0.78/0.39/0.09; SHS 0.60/0.35/0.12; DiMUM 0.17/0.02/0.01 at 1K/2K/5K unlearning steps.
